newsitem.title: UK: Vodafone net new subscribers rise 20 pct in 96.
newsitem.headline: Vodafone net new subscribers rise 20 pct in 96.

text.p: Mobile 'phone company Vodafone Group Plc said on Thursday its overall subscriber base grew by over 20 percent in the UK in 1996, with the addition of more than 468,000 net new subscribers.
At year-end, Vodafone said it had a total UK subscriber base of more than 2.8 million, with over 1.22 million on the digital network.
The 1996 performance reinforced Vodafone's position as the UK market leader in both the overall and the digital market, the company said.

In the October-December quarter, Vodafone added 146,000 net new subscribers in the UK, after connecting some 332,000 subscribers. The quarter was better at gross and net level than the equivalent 1995 period (gross 286,000, net 143,000).

Internationally, Vodafone's share of net new subscribers rose by 148,000. During 1996, Vodafone's share of subscribers almost doubled to 970,000 and the company confirmed its overseas businesses had moved into profit for the first time.
Particularly strong performances were reported in France, Greece and South Africa.
"There was a strong all round performance from Vodafone in 1996," chief executive Chris Gent said in a statement.

"The highlight of the year in the UK was the strong growth in our digital network where the subscriber base increased by 820,000, over 205 per cent, with new connections being supported by a very successful policy of migrating existing customers from the analogue to the digital network," he added.
"Our overseas businesses collectively produced an exceptional performance and continue to go from strength to strength."
